s1.syndrome_frame: Recurrent pustular eruptions on the face with exacerbation by sunlight exposure
salient_findings: Recurrent pustular eruptions on the face
Presence of monomorphous pustules over background erythema on the medial cheeks, chin, and nose
key_facts: 4-year history of recurrent pustular eruptions
Eruptions occur on the face
Mild associated pruritus without burning sensation
Eruptions are intermittent with erythematous papules and prominent pustules
Exacerbation by sunlight exposure, especially in summer months
Resolution within 3-4 days, leaving mild background erythema by 5-7 days
Failed response to broad-spectrum sunscreens, topical/oral antibiotics, and topical ivermectin
No joint pain, fever, fatigue, changes in urine color, medication use, or rashes elsewhere
No significant medical history
Numerous 1-2mm monomorphous pustules over background erythema on medial cheeks, chin, and nose
Negative laboratory tests for antinuclear antibodies, anti-SSA/Ro antibodies, anti-SSB/La antibodies, bacterial swab, and fungal organisms
Histopathology demonstrates intrafollicular and subcorneal pustule formation

shortlist.label: Actinic folliculitis
shortlist.why_kept: Recurrent pustular eruptions on the face with exacerbation by sunlight exposure

shortlist.label: Polymorphic light eruption
shortlist.why_kept: Exacerbation by sunlight exposure, especially in summer months

shortlist.label: Subcorneal pustular dermatosis
shortlist.why_kept: Histopathology demonstrates intrafollicular and subcorneal pustule formation

shortlist.label: Rosacea
shortlist.why_kept: Recurrent pustular eruptions on the face with erythematous papules and prominent pustules

shortlist.label: Eosinophilic pustular folliculitis
shortlist.why_kept: Mild associated pruritus without burning sensation and pustular eruptions

raw.rationale: The patient's history of recurrent pustular eruptions on the face, exacerbated by sunlight exposure, and the presence of intrafollicular and subcorneal pustule formation on histopathology are consistent with actinic folliculitis

rejected.label: Polymorphic light eruption
rejected.why: While it can be exacerbated by sunlight, the presence of intrafollicular and subcorneal pustules is more specific to actinic folliculitis

rejected.label: Subcorneal pustular dermatosis
rejected.why: Typically presents with larger, more superficial pustules and is not specifically exacerbated by sunlight

rejected.label: Rosacea
rejected.why: Usually presents with burning sensation, telangiectasias, and is not typically exacerbated by sunlight to the same degree

rejected.label: Eosinophilic pustular folliculitis
rejected.why: Typically presents with more intense pruritus and eosinophilia on histopathology, which is not mentioned in the case
